claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has been reported in a hierarchical-heterostructured state featuring multilevel chemical fluctuations.
A coarse-grained potential embedding hierarchical structural descriptors can improve prediction accuracy and computational efficiency for HfNbTiVAl10.
The proposed potential can capture the elastic behavior of HfNbTiVAl10.
The proposed potential can capture fracture processes in HfNbTiVAl10.
Atomic chemical fluctuations can be coarse-grained into effective mesoscale hierarchical descriptors.
Those mesoscale descriptors bridge fine-scale chemical ordering to macroscopic mechanical responses.
The model will enable rapid simulation of stress-strain behavior.
The model will simulate crack propagation while retaining the essential physics governing toughness.
The proposed method will be approximately 5–10 times faster than traditional methods.
The proposed method will reduce prediction error from greater than 20% to approximately 10% relative to experiments.
First-principles and molecular-dynamics methods are time-consuming and difficult to use for high-throughput alloy prediction.
CALPHAD modeling can require significant computational resources.
Conventional machine-learning methods are computationally heavy for this prediction task.
Thermophysical-parameter calculations are computationally heavy for this prediction task.
Existing approaches are less reliable for predicting fracture toughness.
The model may lose reliability when its mesoscale descriptors omit critical atomistic interactions at extreme temperatures, high strain rates, or under dynamic loading.
Crack-tip-dominated phenomena may cause the proposed model to lose reliability.
Preliminary evidence suggests that the proposed descriptor-based model will provide efficiency and accuracy gains.
The exact gains and descriptor robustness across deformation modes remain unvalidated.
The hypothesis is falsified if any property prediction deviates from experiment by more than 10% or if the speedup is less than fivefold.
